title: Contour Estimation of Vector Causal Slopes in Partially Linear Models with Non-Gaussian Treatments
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; independent terminal validity confirms downgrade-stop. Math pass and six cited-verified-attested, with unrepaired positioning/ballast findings disclosed.
gap_reasons: tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope

The delivered result is uniform K/n coefficient risk on the explicit sufficient regime, with matching estimator and honest-ball lower bounds only for K^2≤n. The framing correctly leaves necessity near linear dimension and sharpness of the code-error budget open; neither is established by the Bernstein calculation. Literature positioning is stale: the scalar-contour predecessor has public identification and minimax theorem text, rather than being merely an internal conceptual proposal ([CausalSmith, Theorems 2–3](https://causalsmith.org/papers/stat_sa_plm_cumulant_converse_nongaussian_spectral_annihilation/paper.pdf)). The honest-ball benchmark adds standard Gaussian testing and Markov coverage, without distributional calibration or efficiency results. The projected score is constrained by this specialized extension, the unresolved joint dimension/code-error characterization, and the absence of an implementation or supporting evidence establishing practical utility despite the enormous bank and calibration constants. proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved an informal uniform K/n risk bound for the observable jointly truncated contour estimator on an explicit sufficient regime containing every K^2<=n pair and eventually every fixed power-sublinear sequence. Same-class minimax risk and conservative all-honest-ball radius brackets match on K^2<=n; the math review passes and all six citations are verified-attested. Independent terminal validity confirms incremental novelty below the required field floor; near-linear necessity, sharp code-error limits and approximation-adaptive slopes remain open, and no Lean or F-stage certification was attempted.
tldr: An imperfect treatment code and no outcome code suffice for estimating an exact vector basis of causal slopes under independent additive innovations and fixed non-Gaussian treatment separation. Joint observable truncation preserves the residual vector variance, while an operator Bernstein bound controls failed inverse certification. The main result proves uniform squared coefficient risk \(C^\dagger K/n\) on the explicitly defined sufficient set \(\mathcal A_\dagger\). It includes every \(K^2\le n\) pair and, for each fixed \(\gamma>0\), all sufficiently large samples with \(K\le n^{1-\gamma}\). On \(K^2\le n\), same-class Gaussian-outcome testing gives matching estimator and all-honest-Euclidean-ball lower bounds. The reported coefficient ball is the conservative Markov corollary of risk. The residual dimension question concerns necessity or sharpness of the sufficient regime and inverse certification near the linear boundary. A construction-specific limitation would require a separate argument from an all-estimator impossibility claim.
gap: Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis (2025, Section 7) leave distribution-aware heterogeneous-effect estimation as a future direction. Their scalar ACE guarantees do not supply a coupled basis matrix, total same-sample certification, or an all-honest-ball benchmark. The internal scalar contour and heterogeneous-band proposals already occupy the transform idea and broad heterogeneous-inference narrative.
fill: The formal claims isolate the derived baseline envelope, residue stability, Hilbert moments, fixed numerical margins, fallback loss and same-class testing as separate proof obligations. The complete benchmark is deliberately a modest methods contribution. The operator-norm dimension question identifies the part that is not settled by auditing the presolve.
